Verdict: ACCEPT, with two minor exposition fixesThe extension is mathematically sound under its stated hypotheses. I find:no in-hypothesis counterexample to the nonnegative partial-source phase lemma;no reuse of a physical donor in the aggregation or weighted ledger;no failure in the arbitrary- $a$  filling;no contradiction with the universal coefficient-one target.The sharp family does refute the proposed local rule that every source touching a cavity supplies two units. It does not refute the global target, because the family has  $a$  foreign sources touching one root cavity while the number of root cavities is still one, and the theorem never identifies “touching” with “earning two units.”Two statements should be made more explicit for a fully self-contained written proof:every unlisted vertex outside  $C$  is blank except for the prescribed source supports and explicitly added flank selections;the removed even-row patch sites are optional filler selections, not prescribed source supports.Those are clarity gaps. I do not find a mathematical defect.1. Boundary accounting remains exact for escaping componentsThe root boundary calculation survives the loss of component containment.The two extreme columns still contain exactly the  $h$  prescribed inside supports on each side, hence exactly  $2h$  retained selections altogether. Every other site in those columns is forced blank by one of:the next inside support at the first row;the preceding inside support at each later even row;the axial support at the final row.The same support argument excludes an endpoint in either extreme column. This argument concerns the root source and feasibility only; a foreign source escaping through another boundary does not change it.The original cavity partition and the trimmed shifted partition are unions of complete row/column pairs in their respective phase frames. Consequently:every original endpoint square lying in  $C$  is wholly contained in  $C$ ;every shifted endpoint square after trimming is wholly contained in  $C$ ;a matching edge of a partial component may cross the cavity boundary without changing the raw square count.Thus the exact partition relation remains
$$D_C-D'_C
=
2+\sum_K\bigl(E_C(K)-E'_C(K)\bigr).$$
This is a raw-excess identity. It does not assign a corrected whole-receiver charge to a component that leaves  $C$ , and it does not treat a shifted square as a donor.The fact that a forcing support may lie outside  $C$  causes no problem. The receiver square containing the endpoint is still complete, and the outside support can force the required interior label.2. Parallel partial sources have nonnegative phaseThe parallel case is correctly separated from the fully enclosed case.For a positive-phase parallel source:chamber squares have zero raw excess in both partitions;nonterminal arm squares have zero raw excess in both partitions;each actual physical terminal tip tile in  $C$  contributes
$$+\frac12-\left(-\frac12\right)=1.$$
Therefore
$$\Gamma_C(K)
=
E_C(K)-E'_C(K)
=
\#\{\text{physical terminal tip tiles of }K\text{ lying in }C\}.$$
The possible values are  $0,1,2$ .A vertical arm can cross the top or bottom of  $C$ . If the portion inside  $C$  contains no actual terminal tip, its arm bands contribute zero. If an actual tip lies in  $C$ , the positive physical tip label and negative shifted tip label give one unit.A horizontal chamber or arm cannot cross an endpoint-free extreme column. Any connected source path that crossed such a side would contain an endpoint in the prohibited boundary column. Therefore the source cannot acquire an artificial side cut in a row band. This covers the case in which a horizontal arm meets  $C$ : either the complete relevant arm segment, including its actual tip, lies between the extreme columns, or the source has no endpoint there.The phase statement is therefore conditional on the declared positive alignment. The earlier potential objections remain outside the hypotheses:a one-column translation changes the source’s original phase and gives raw charge  $-1$ ;an even-constant row reflection changes the row-pair phase.The permitted even translations and odd-constant pair-preserving reflections retain the  $+1$  whole-source phase and the row-band tables.A partial source can also have a matching edge from an endpoint inside  $C$  to an endpoint outside  $C$ . That edge affects neither  $E_C(K)$  nor  $E'_C(K)$ , because those quantities are raw sums over endpoint squares. No partial corrected charge is being claimed.3. Perpendicular partial sources have nonnegative row-band gainsThe perpendicular case is also correct, provided the source remains in the declared positive phase and all endpoints meeting  $C$  belong to the prescribed source component.Because the cavity boundary consists of complete physical row pairs, an intersecting source is divided only into:a complete two-row interior chamber band;an actual end row paired with its exterior neighbor.There is no artificial one-row endpoint band created by the cavity cut.Interior bandLet  $a$  be the number of selected outer-flank sites in the left shifted endpoint square and  $b$  the number of selected inner-flank sites in the right shifted endpoint square.Each shifted endpoint square has  $p=2$ , so its raw excess is
$$e=a-1
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
e=b-1.$$
The two-square shifted contribution is therefore
$$-2+a+b.$$
The physical contribution of the corresponding two-row chamber band is zero. Hence the band phase gain is
$$2-a-b.$$
Each flank has two sites in the band, and both sites cannot be selected:each flank site already sees its adjacent chamber endpoint;if both were selected, each would acquire a second occupied neighbor.Thus
$$a\le1,\qquad b\le1,$$
and the interior gain is nonnegative.An endpoint on one of these flanks would be adjacent to the prescribed source endpoint and would join the source component. Since the source component is complete and prescribed, such a foreign endpoint is excluded by the component hypotheses.Cap bandA cap has one chamber-side shifted square of type
$$(p,t)=(1,1+a_{\mathrm{cap}}),$$
where  $a_{\mathrm{cap}}\in\{0,1\}$  is the optional outer-flank selection. Its raw excess is
$$-\frac12+a_{\mathrm{cap}}.$$
The other arm square has type  $(p,t)=(2,1)$ , hence raw excess zero. The physical cap contribution is  $+\frac12$ , so the cap gain is
$$1-a_{\mathrm{cap}}\ge0.$$
If an end-row horizontal arm enters  $C$ , it cannot cross an endpoint-free extreme column. Therefore it either terminates in the cavity with its actual tip, in which case the established arm-tip table applies, or it does not contribute an endpoint path inside  $C$ .Summing all actual bands gives
$$\Gamma_C(K)\ge0.$$
When the source is fully enclosed, the whole-flank exclusions strengthen this to
$$\Gamma_C(K)\ge2.$$
For a partial source, that stronger bound is unavailable in general. The extension correctly distinguishes these cases.4. The exact open-source ledger has no hidden donor reuseDefine
$$G_C=\sum_{\text{nonroot prescribed sources }K}\Gamma_C(K).$$
The partial-source lemma gives
$$G_C\ge0.$$
Let  $\Phi_C$  be the signed membership of complete-comb singleton end tiles:
$$\Phi_C
=
\sum_K
\bigl(
\mathbf 1[U_K\in C]-\mathbf 1[S_K\in C]
\bigr).$$
The componentwise raw identity then gives
$$D_C
=
2+G_C+\Phi_C+D'_C,
\qquad
G_C\ge0,\quad D'_C\ge0.$$
Only complete-comb end membership can contribute a negative term. A partial prescribed source contributes zero or positive phase.For several cavities, if every original positive no-endpoint donor belongs to at most  $c$  cavities, then
$$2N+G+\Phi
\le
\sum_jD_{C_j}
\le
cD_{\mathrm{all}},$$
and hence
$$c\Delta
\ge
2N+G+\Phi-cB+cE.$$
The upper bound is literal physical incidence:each  $D_{C_j}$  counts original physical no-endpoint tiles;a tile is counted at most  $c$  times;shifted squares are not counted in  $D_{\mathrm{all}}$ ; $G$  and  $\Phi$  are phase terms in the exact identities, not additional donor supplies.The weighted form is also valid. If
$$\sum_{j:Q\in C_j}\lambda_j\le1$$
for every positive physical donor  $Q$ , then
$$\Delta
\ge
-B+
\sum_j\lambda_j(2+G_{C_j}+\Phi_{C_j})
+E.$$
This is the correct way to combine overlapping cavities. Counting a source in multiple phase identities does not count any physical donor multiple times.The  $c=2$  integrality consequence is valid. If  $N=B$  and  $\Phi\ge-1$ , then
$$2\Delta\ge-1,$$
and integer-valued  $\Delta$  implies  $\Delta\ge0$ .5. Partial-contact normalization remains applicableThe normalization argument applies to partial sources because freezing is a property of the complete prescribed source component, not of its relation to  $C$ .Every endpoint component meeting  $C$  is assumed to be one of:a prescribed positive source, possibly extending outside  $C$ ;a prescribed complete comb, possibly extending outside  $C$ .All such components are frozen. Normalization:promotes an existing endpoint;removes its matching mate from the endpoint set;creates no new endpoint;retains old selections.Therefore it cannot change the endpoint labels in  $C$ , cannot move an exterior endpoint into  $C$ , and cannot turn a partial source into a different component. The raw phase calculation remains valid after normalization.The separate outside nonpositive-receiver hypothesis is still needed for the global  $E\ge0$  ledger term. The partial-contact theorem does not remove that requirement.6. Audit of the all- $a$  sharp obstruction familyThe explicit family is consistent for all stated parameters
$$a\ge1,\quad H\ge3,\quad W\ge32a,\quad V\ge2H+2,$$
with  $W,V$  even.The root cavity is
$$C=\{4,\ldots,y+1\}\times\{4,\ldots,W+1\},
\qquad y=2H+4.$$
Its physical row pairs are
$$(4,5),\ldots,(y,y+1),$$
and its physical column pairs are
$$(4,5),\ldots,(W,W+1).$$
For source  $i$ ,
$$c_i=14+32i$$
is even, so the source has the required perpendicular positive phase. Its chamber rows are  $7,\ldots,V+6$ , with upper arm row  $7$  inside  $C$  and lower arm row  $V+6$  outside  $C$ , since
$$V+6\ge y+4.$$
The source/support envelope is contained in the six-column interval
$$[c_i-1,c_i+5].$$
Different envelopes are 32 columns apart, leaving 25 intervening columns. They cannot interact with one another or with the root arms under the stated  $W$ -bound.Phase inside  $C$ The upper cap has one outer flank selection, so its gain is
$$1-1=0.$$
Every intersecting interior chamber band has exactly one outer flank and one inner flank selection, so its gain is
$$2-1-1=0.$$
The lower arm and lower cap are outside  $C$ . Therefore each foreign source has
$$\Gamma_C(K)=0,$$
and hence
$$G_C=0.$$
There are no combs, so
$$\Phi_C=0.$$
Feasibility interfacesThe periodic patch has the required local behavior.At the upper arm:row  $6$  has the prescribed support selections at  $c,c+2,c+4$ ;row  $7$  has the source endpoints and the flank selections at  $c-1,c+5$ ;each support sees exactly its intended endpoint.At the first chamber band:the row- $8$  filler at  $c+3$  is retained or added as required by the arm-support table;the row- $9$  flank selections see their chamber endpoints or their isolated filler partner;no selected site acquires a second occupied neighbor.The same pattern repeats through all interior chamber bands. The  $y/y+1$  band is still an interior source band, because the source chamber continues beyond  $C$ . At the  $y+1/y+2$  transition, the selected sites in the last cavity row have no foreign selected neighbor below them. The next prescribed flank selections begin on the appropriate odd rows.The lower arm is at least four rows below the cavity boundary. Its support envelope therefore cannot interact with the final cavity-row selections.The only point that should be stated explicitly is that the sites removed from the even-row base pattern,
$$c,\ c+2,\ c+4,$$
are optional filler selections. They are not prescribed source supports. The prescribed arm supports at rows  $6$  and  $8$  are retained.Physical deficitAway from the source patches, every no-endpoint physical tile has two selections except for the two final-band tiles
$$\{6,7\},
\qquad
\{W,W+1\},$$
which each have one selection.Inside a source patch, the physical tile containing source endpoints is excluded from  $D_C$ . Its neighboring no-endpoint tiles retain two selections. For example, in an ordinary chamber band:the tile with columns  $c+2,c+3$  has the two selections at upper  $c+3$  and lower  $c+2$ ;the tile with columns  $c+4,c+5$  has the two selections at lower  $c+4$  and lower  $c+5$ .The same local check works in the upper arm band and at the final cavity band.Therefore the only physical deficit-one tiles are the two final-band tiles, and
$$D_C=2.$$
Shifted deficitEvery shifted no-endpoint square has two selections.At an ordinary patch, the shifted endpoint pairs containing source endpoints are excluded. The neighboring no-endpoint pairs have two selections, for example:
$$(\text{upper},c+3)+(\text{lower},c+4),$$
and
$$(\text{lower},c+5)+(\text{upper},c+6).$$
The unaffected shifted pairs retain the alternating two-selection pattern. Hence
$$D'_C=0.$$
The family therefore satisfies
$$G_C=\Phi_C=D'_C=0,
\qquad
D_C=2.$$
The proposed local rule
$$D_C\ge2(1+\text{number of foreign sources touching }C)$$
would demand  $2(a+1)$ , while the actual value is  $2$ . The overclaim is  $2a$ , arbitrarily large.That is a counterexample to the touched-source allocation rule only. It does not imply
$$\Delta<0,$$
and it does not disprove the global coefficient-one target. No global target failure is established or claimed.7. Actual false statements versus proof gapsActual false statementI find no false mathematical statement in the corrected theorem under its hypotheses.The only wording that could mislead is the phrase that the source’s “whole phase gain is two.” The relevant cavity phase is instead
$$\Gamma_C(K)=0$$
for each partial source in the sharp family; the value two belongs to the source’s fully enclosed whole-flank calculation. The surrounding text makes that distinction, but it should be repeated once near equation (6).Minor proof-writing gapsTwo details should be made explicit:Complete the finite configuration by declaring every unlisted outside- $C$  vertex blank, except for prescribed source supports and the listed sharp-flank selections.State directly from the rotated source label table that the even-row sites removed by each patch are optional filler selections and are not prescribed supports.Neither point produces a counterexample. The natural blank extension satisfies the feasibility checks, and the support table supplies the retained source supports.Final assessmentACCEPT.The new theorem correctly proves:nonnegative phase for every prescribed partial source in either direction;exact raw cavity aggregation with no donor reuse;correct normalization preservation for partial contacts;failure of automatic two-unit credit for merely touched sources;an explicit feasible all- $a$  family with
$$D_C=2,\qquad G_C=\Phi_C=D'_C=0.$$
The family defeats the local source-touch allocation rule, while leaving the universal coefficient-one target untouched.
